questions.q: In the sentence 'The new manager was affable and easy to approach', the word 'affable' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Friendly. Affable: pleasant and good-natured.

questions.q: Choose the phrase with the correct order of adjectives: 'She bought ____.'
o: a beautiful old Indian silk sari
an old beautiful Indian silk sari
an Indian beautiful old silk sari
a silk beautiful old Indian sari
questions.x: Correct answer: a beautiful old Indian silk sari. Order: opinion – age – origin – material.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech: "Let us wait for the results," she said.
o: She said let us wait for the results.
She suggested that let them wait for the results.
She ordered them to wait for the results.
She suggested that they should wait for the results.
questions.x: 'Let us' as a proposal is reported with 'suggested/proposed that … should'.

questions.q: The clerk was accused ____ leaking the confidential report.
questions.x: One is accused of something.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Many a worker / have lost his job / because of the lockout.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'have lost his job'. 'Many a' takes a singular verb: 'has lost his job'.

questions.q: In the sentence 'The spokesperson tried to obfuscate the issue with technical jargon', the word 'obfuscate' means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Make unclear. Obfuscate: to confuse or obscure.

questions.q: Officials declined to comment because the matter was ____.
questions.x: Sub judice: under judicial consideration.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
Neither he / nor I / are responsible for the delay.
questions.x: The error is in part (c): 'are responsible for the delay'. The verb agrees with the nearer subject 'I': 'am responsible'.

questions.q: Hardly ____ the audit begun when the auditor fell ill.
questions.x: 'Hardly had … when' with inversion.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Neither of the two proposals (were) acceptable to the board.
questions.x: Correct answer: was. 'Neither of' takes a singular verb in formal English.

questions.q: In the sentence 'She burnt the midnight oil to finish the audit report', the idiom means:
questions.x: Correct answer: Worked late into the night. It refers to working late at night.

questions.q:
Choose the best replacement for the bracketed part of the sentence. If no change is needed, choose 'No improvement'.
Ten kilometres (are) a long distance to walk every day.
questions.x: A distance taken as one amount takes a singular verb.

questions.q: According to the passage, one drawback of sea walls is that they:
o: May transfer erosion to nearby stretches of coast
questions.x: Answer: 'May transfer erosion to nearby stretches of coast'. This is stated in the first sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Sea walls protect coasts, but they can also shift erosion to the next beach along the shore. Mangroves and sand dunes, by contrast, absorb wave energy, trap sediment and recover after storms. They also support fisheries on which coastal families depend. Yet they are often cleared for ports, resorts and aquaculture because their benefits are spread across many people while the profits from clearing them go to a few.

questions.q: Why are mangroves often cleared, according to the passage?
o: Their benefits are widely spread while gains from clearing go to a few
questions.x: Answer: 'Their benefits are widely spread while gains from clearing go to a few'. This is explained in the last sentence. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Sea walls protect coasts, but they can also shift erosion to the next beach along the shore. Mangroves and sand dunes, by contrast, absorb wave energy, trap sediment and recover after storms. They also support fisheries on which coastal families depend. Yet they are often cleared for ports, resorts and aquaculture because their benefits are spread across many people while the profits from clearing them go to a few.

questions.q: The passage presents mangroves and dunes as:
o: Weaker than sea walls in every respect
Natural defences with additional economic benefits
questions.x: Answer: 'Natural defences with additional economic benefits'. They absorb wave energy and support fisheries. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Sea walls protect coasts, but they can also shift erosion to the next beach along the shore. Mangroves and sand dunes, by contrast, absorb wave energy, trap sediment and recover after storms. They also support fisheries on which coastal families depend. Yet they are often cleared for ports, resorts and aquaculture because their benefits are spread across many people while the profits from clearing them go to a few.

questions.q: According to the passage, why is a delayed payout of limited use?
o: It cannot fund inputs needed for the next season
It is usually smaller than the premium
It causes inflation in rural areas
It is paid only to large farmers
questions.x: Answer: 'It cannot fund inputs needed for the next season'. A late payout 'cannot buy seed for the next sowing'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Crop insurance is meant to protect farmers from ruin in bad seasons, but its value depends on how quickly and fairly claims are settled. A payout that arrives a year late cannot buy seed for the next sowing. Estimating losses through a few crop-cutting experiments may miss local damage, leaving some farmers uncompensated while others in the same district are paid. Technology such as satellite imagery and weather data can narrow these gaps, but only if the results are trusted by farmers and insurers alike.

questions.q: What weakness of loss estimation does the passage mention?
o: A small number of crop-cutting experiments may miss local damage
Insurers do not have any data
questions.x: Answer: 'A small number of crop-cutting experiments may miss local damage'. Few experiments may not reflect damage at the local level. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Crop insurance is meant to protect farmers from ruin in bad seasons, but its value depends on how quickly and fairly claims are settled. A payout that arrives a year late cannot buy seed for the next sowing. Estimating losses through a few crop-cutting experiments may miss local damage, leaving some farmers uncompensated while others in the same district are paid. Technology such as satellite imagery and weather data can narrow these gaps, but only if the results are trusted by farmers and insurers alike.

questions.q: The author's view of technology in crop insurance is best described as:
o: Hopeful but conditional on mutual trust
questions.x: Answer: 'Hopeful but conditional on mutual trust'. It can help 'but only if the results are trusted'. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Crop insurance is meant to protect farmers from ruin in bad seasons, but its value depends on how quickly and fairly claims are settled. A payout that arrives a year late cannot buy seed for the next sowing. Estimating losses through a few crop-cutting experiments may miss local damage, leaving some farmers uncompensated while others in the same district are paid. Technology such as satellite imagery and weather data can narrow these gaps, but only if the results are trusted by farmers and insurers alike.

questions.q: Arrange the following Acts in chronological order: 1. Pitt's India Act 2. Regulating Act 3. Charter Act (abolishing Company's trade monopoly in India) 4. Government of India Act transferring rule to the Crown
questions.x: Regulating Act (1773), Pitt's India Act (1784), Charter Act (1813), GoI Act (1858).

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Indian National Congress sessions:
1. The 1907 Surat session saw the split between Moderates and Extremists.
2. The 1916 Lucknow session reunited them.
3. The 1929 Lahore session adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Swaraj Party:
1. It was formed by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru.
2. It advocated entry into legislative councils to obstruct them from within.
3. Gandhi opposed its formation and expelled its leaders from the Congress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Gandhi accepted the Swarajists' programme in 1924; there was no expulsion.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. It provided for two independent dominions, India and Pakistan.
2. The Constituent Assemblies were empowered to frame constitutions and also act as legislatures.
3. It retained the British Crown's paramountcy over princely states.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Paramountcy lapsed; princely states were free to accede.

questions.q: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Swadeshi Movement (1905–11)?
o: Mass non-payment of land revenue throughout India
Use of traditional festivals for mobilisation
questions.x: Correct answer: Mass non-payment of land revenue throughout India. Non-payment of revenue was not part of the Swadeshi programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Subsidiary Alliance:
1. It was devised by Lord Wellesley.
2. Hyderabad was among the first states to accept it.
3. A ruler who accepted it remained free to conduct his own foreign relations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The ruler surrendered control of foreign relations, kept a British force at his own cost and accepted a Resident.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Revolt of 1857:
1. Bahadur Shah Zafar was proclaimed emperor by the rebels at Delhi.
2. Lord Canning was the Governor-General at the time.
3. Madras and Bombay presidencies were the main centres of the revolt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The main centres were in north and central India (Delhi, Kanpur, Lucknow, Jhansi, Bihar).

questions.q:
Which of the following happened during Lord Curzon's tenure as Viceroy?
1. Partition of Bengal
2. Ancient Monuments Preservation Act
3. Indian Universities Act
4. Morley–Minto reforms
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Morley–Minto reforms came in 1909 under Lord Minto.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Akbar's policy of Sulh-i-kul promoted religious tolerance.
Reason (R): Akbar abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; abolition of jizya was one measure, but Sulh-i-kul is a broader principle of universal peace.

questions.q:
Match the cave site with its dominant religious association:
Site:
A. Ajanta
B. Ellora
C. Elephanta
D. Udayagiri–Khandagiri
Association:
1. Buddhist, Hindu and Jain
2. Hindu (Shaiva)
3. Jain
4. Buddhist
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Ajanta) → 4 (Buddhist); B (Ellora) → 1 (Buddhist, Hindu and Jain); C (Elephanta) → 2 (Hindu (Shaiva)); D (Udayagiri–Khandagiri) → 3 (Jain).
Rock-cut architecture in India.

questions.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.x: Correct answer: Sufi order — Chishti — Khwaja Moinuddin (Ajmer). Nizamuddin Auliya and Baba Farid were Chishti saints.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about B. R. Ambedkar is NOT correct?
o: He founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
He presided over the Karachi session of the Congress
He attended all three Round Table Conferences
questions.x: Correct answer: He presided over the Karachi session of the Congress. Vallabhbhai Patel presided over the Karachi session (1931).

questions.q:
Match the bilateral exercise with India's partner country:
Exercise:
A. Ajeya Warrior
B. Harimau Shakti
C. Khanjar
D. Lamitiye
Partner:
1. Seychelles
2. Malaysia
3. United Kingdom
4. Kyrgyzstan
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Ajeya Warrior) → 3 (United Kingdom); B (Harimau Shakti) → 2 (Malaysia); C (Khanjar) → 4 (Kyrgyzstan); D (Lamitiye) → 1 (Seychelles).
Each is a recurring bilateral army exercise.

questions.q: Which of the following combinations correctly describes the EPFO's auto-settlement reform of 2025?
o: All claims to be settled only at regional offices
Limit for auto-settled advance claims raised to ₹5 lakh, cutting settlement time without manual checks
questions.x: Correct answer: Limit for auto-settled advance claims raised to ₹5 lakh, cutting settlement time without manual checks. The limit was raised from ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh.

questions.q: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: D. Gukesh — youngest undisputed World Chess Champion (December 2024)
Neeraj Chopra — Olympic gold at Paris 2024
Indian hockey team — silver at Paris 2024
questions.x: Neeraj won silver at Paris; Manu Bhaker won two bronzes; hockey won bronze.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025:
1. It proposes removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Ministers or ministers held in custody for 30 consecutive days on serious charges.
2. It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
3. It was passed by both Houses in the same session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
It was referred to a JPC.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana:
1. It covers jobs created between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027.
2. It is implemented through EPFO.
3. Employers in all sectors get incentives for six years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Employer incentives are for two years (extended to four years for manufacturing).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India's working-age share of population will keep rising for the next two decades or so.
Reason (R): India's total fertility rate has fallen below the replacement level of 2.1.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both are true; the rising working-age share reflects past births, while below-replacement fertility will later reduce it.

questions.q:
Consider the following about wildlife conservation in 2025:
1. Madhav National Park in Madhya Pradesh was notified as a tiger reserve.
2. Cheetahs were released in Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as a second home after Kuno.
3. Khichan and Menar in Rajasthan were designated Ramsar sites.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three happened in 2025.

questions.q:
The World Bank's 2025 poverty brief placed India among the more equal countries by its Gini index. Consider the following:
1. India's Gini index was about 25.5.
2. The ranking was based on income inequality.
3. The brief also noted a sharp fall in extreme poverty between 2011-12 and 2022-23.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect; Statement 3 is correct.
The Gini estimate is consumption-based; income inequality is usually much higher than consumption inequality.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Indus Waters Treaty:
1. It was signed in 1960 with the World Bank as a signatory.
2. Waters of the eastern rivers — Ravi, Beas and Sutlej — are allocated to India.
3. India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
The western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) are allocated largely to Pakistan.

questions.q:
Match the leader with the office assumed in 2025:
Leader:
A. Friedrich Merz
B. Mark Carney
C. Sanae Takaichi
D. Sushila Karki
Office:
1. Chancellor of Germany
2. Interim Prime Minister of Nepal
3. Prime Minister of Canada
4. Prime Minister of Japan
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Friedrich Merz) → 1 (Chancellor of Germany); B (Mark Carney) → 3 (Prime Minister of Canada); C (Sanae Takaichi) → 4 (Prime Minister of Japan); D (Sushila Karki) → 2 (Interim Prime Minister of Nepal).
All assumed office in 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following about NVS-02, launched in January 2025:
1. It was launched by GSLV-F15, the 100th launch from Sriharikota.
2. It is part of the NavIC navigation constellation.
3. It reached its intended orbit exactly as planned.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
A valve problem prevented the planned orbit-raising after launch.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Income-tax Act, 2025:
1. It replaces the separate 'previous year' and 'assessment year' with a single 'tax year'.
2. It was intended mainly to simplify language and structure, with far fewer sections than the 1961 Act.
3. It changed the income-tax slab rates for all taxpayers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Rates continue to be set through the annual Finance Act; the new Act was presented as a simplification.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Parliament cannot amend the basic structure of the Constitution.
Reason (R): In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the Supreme Court held that the amending power under Article 368 does not extend to destroying the basic structure.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
Consider the following about State Legislative Councils:
1. Parliament can create or abolish a Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by special majority.
2. Such a law is not treated as an amendment of the Constitution for Article 368.
3. A Governor can abolish the Council by an executive order.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Creation or abolition is under Article 169 by a law of Parliament.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Union Territories:
1. Delhi has a Legislative Assembly under Article 239AA.
2. Ladakh is a Union Territory without a legislature.
3. Chandigarh has a Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Chandigarh has no legislature.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Rajya Sabha has special powers to authorise Parliament to legislate on a State List matter.
Reason (R): Under Article 249, it can pass a resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting declaring such legislation necessary in the national interest.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: Correct answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. R explains A.

questions.q:
In which of the following can a joint sitting of Parliament NOT be held?
1. A Money Bill
2. A Constitution Amendment Bill
3. An ordinary Bill rejected by the other House
4. A Financial Bill under Article 117(1)
How many of the above?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Joint sittings are barred for Money Bills and Constitution Amendment Bills.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Attorney General of India:
1. The President appoints a person qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.
2. The Attorney General can speak in either House of Parliament but cannot vote.
3. The Attorney General is a member of the Union Cabinet.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Attorney General is not a member of the Cabinet.

questions.q:
Which of the following subjects were transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment?
1. Education
2. Forests
3. Protection of wild animals and birds
4. Agriculture
How many of the above?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Education, forests, wildlife protection, weights and measures and administration of justice were moved; agriculture remains a State subject.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court:
1. Disputes between the Centre and States fall under its original jurisdiction under Article 131.
2. Under Article 143, the President may seek its advisory opinion.
3. Its advisory opinion is binding on the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Advisory opinions are not binding.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Lokpal:
1. It was established under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013.
2. The Prime Minister is within its jurisdiction, subject to safeguards.
3. It is a constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Lokpal is statutory.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Right to Information Act, 2005:
1. The Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee headed by the Prime Minister.
2. Information relating to the life or liberty of a person is to be provided within 48 hours.
3. The 2019 amendment allowed the Central Government to prescribe the term and salary of Information Commissioners.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Directive Principles of State Policy:
1. They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
2. Courts cannot enforce them directly.
3. A law implementing Articles 39(b) or 39(c) is protected under Article 31C from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Article 31C protects such laws (the broader 42nd Amendment extension was struck down in Minerva Mills).

questions.q:
Match the Article with its financial provision:
Article:
A. Article 266
B. Article 267
C. Article 275
D. Article 282
Provision:
1. Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts
2. Contingency Fund
3. Discretionary grants by the Union or a State for any public purpose
4. Statutory grants-in-aid to States
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Article 266) → 1 (Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts); B (Article 267) → 2 (Contingency Fund); C (Article 275) → 4 (Statutory grants-in-aid to States); D (Article 282) → 3 (Discretionary grants by the Union or a State for any public purpose).
Key Articles in Part XII.

questions.q: If income inequality in a country falls, which change is expected?
o: The Lorenz curve moves away from the line of equality
The Lorenz curve moves closer to the line of equality and the Gini coefficient falls
questions.x: Correct answer: The Lorenz curve moves closer to the line of equality and the Gini coefficient falls. A lower Gini indicates more equal distribution.

questions.q: Nominal GDP of a country is ₹2,56,450 crore and real GDP (at base-year prices) is ₹2,23,000 crore. The GDP deflator is:
questions.x:
GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100 = (2,56,450 / 2,23,000) × 100 = 115.
Prices have risen 15% over the base year.

questions.q: If the fiscal deficit is 4.4% of GDP and interest payments are 3.6% of GDP, the primary deficit is:
questions.x: Correct answer: 0.8% of GDP. Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments.

questions.q:
Consider the following about India's trade agreements:
1. The India–EFTA TEPA includes a commitment to promote investment of US$ 100 billion in India over 15 years.
2. The India–UK CETA was signed in 2025 and includes a Double Contribution Convention on social security.
3. India is a member of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
India opted out of RCEP in 2019.

questions.q: A partner withdrew ₹2,500 at the middle of every month during the year. Interest on drawings is charged at 12% p.a. The interest on drawings is:
questions.x:
Total drawings = 12 × 2,500 = ₹30,000.
Average period for monthly drawings made at the middle of each month = 6 months.
Interest = 30,000 × 12% × 6/12 = ₹1,800.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹40,000 is depreciated at 15% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 3 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 40,000 × (0.85)^3 = ₹24,565.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹22,000.)

questions.q:
Consider the following about the CAG of India:
1. The CAG is appointed by the President under Article 148.
2. The CAG's reports on Union accounts are submitted to the President, who lays them before Parliament.
3. The CAG audits the accounts of all private limited companies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The CAG audits government companies and bodies funded by government, not all private companies.

questions.q: A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹2,50,000 and at the end ₹3,40,000. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹15,000 and withdrew ₹15,000 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 3,40,000 + 15,000 − 15,000 − 2,50,000 = ₹90,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q:
Match the Ind AS with its subject:
Standard:
A. Ind AS 2
B. Ind AS 16
C. Ind AS 115
D. Ind AS 116
Subject:
1. Revenue from contracts with customers
2. Inventories
3. Leases
4. Property, plant and equipment
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Ind AS 2) → 2 (Inventories); B (Ind AS 16) → 4 (Property, plant and equipment); C (Ind AS 115) → 1 (Revenue from contracts with customers); D (Ind AS 116) → 3 (Leases).
Key Ind AS numbers.

questions.q: Salary for March ₹12,000 is outstanding, and insurance of ₹6,000 includes ₹1,500 prepaid. If these adjustments are ignored, net profit will be:
questions.x: Ignoring outstanding salary overstates profit by ₹12,000; ignoring prepaid insurance understates profit by ₹1,500. Net overstatement = ₹10,500.

questions.q: Purchase of office furniture for ₹25,000 on credit from Rajan was entered in the purchases book. The trial balance:
o: Will agree, because it is an error of principle
Will agree only after a suspense account is opened
questions.x: Both debit (Purchases) and credit (Rajan) are recorded; only the head is wrong — an error of principle.

questions.q:
Which of the following are fundamental accounting assumptions under AS 1?
1. Going concern
2. Consistency
3. Accrual
4. Conservatism
How many of the above are fundamental accounting assumptions?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
AS 1 names going concern, consistency and accrual; prudence is a consideration in selecting policies, not a fundamental assumption.

questions.q: A firm earns an average profit of ₹87,000 on capital employed of ₹9,00,000. The normal rate of return in the industry is 8%. Goodwill at 3 years' purchase of super profit is:
Current ratio is 2.5 : 1 and quick ratio 1.5 : 1. If current liabilities are ₹80,000, inventory (the only non-quick current asset) is:

Which of the following were permissible deductions under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936?
1. Deductions for absence from duty
2. Deductions for house accommodation supplied by the employer
3. Deductions for recovery of loans from a welfare fund, subject to conditions
4. Deductions as a general penalty at the employer's discretion without any notified acts or omissions
How many of the above were permissible?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Section 7 allowed specified deductions; arbitrary penalties were never authorised.

questions.q: A factory (120 workers) pays a worker ₹700 per day. The worker is laid off for 30 working days in a year due to power shortage. Lay-off compensation payable is:
questions.x: 50% of basic + DA for days of lay-off: 0.5 × 700 × 30 = ₹10,500.

questions.q: Which statement about 'disguised unemployment' is correct?
o: It is captured fully by the PLFS unemployment rate
Removing some workers would not reduce total output, because their marginal productivity is near zero
It arises when workers move between jobs
questions.x: Disguised unemployment hides inside employment, mostly in family agriculture.

questions.q: A firm's separations during the year were 60 and the average workforce was 400. The labour turnover rate (separation method) is:

Consider the following pairs of Code and subsumed law:
1. Code on Wages — Payment of Bonus Act
2. IR Code — Trade Unions Act
3. Code on Social Security — Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act
4. OSH Code — Plantations Labour Act
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.x:
3 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
The Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act went into the OSH Code.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the 'Decent Work Agenda' of the ILO?
o: Four pillars — employment creation, rights at work, social protection and social dialogue — with gender equality as a cross-cutting goal
A minimum wage set by the ILO for all countries
A WTO agreement on labour standards
questions.x: Correct answer: Four pillars — employment creation, rights at work, social protection and social dialogue — with gender equality as a cross-cutting goal. Introduced in 1999 under Director-General Juan Somavía.

questions.q: Which pair of laws, now subsumed in the Code on Wages, earlier had DIFFERENT wage ceilings for coverage, a gap the Code removes by universal coverage?
o: Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 and Trade Unions Act, 1926
Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (wage ceiling for coverage) and Minimum Wages Act, 1948 (scheduled employments)
Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and Factories Act, 1948
questions.x: Payment of Wages applied only up to a notified wage ceiling and Minimum Wages only to scheduled employments; the Code extends both protections to all employees.

questions.q: A union calls a strike in a private hospital without notice. Under the IR Code, the strike is:
o: Legal, as hospitals are not public utility services under the Code
Legal if more than half the workers join
Illegal, because notice is required in all industrial establishments
Illegal only if the hospital is a government hospital
questions.x: The IR Code's notice requirement (Section 62) covers every industrial establishment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013:
1. An Internal Committee is required in every workplace with ten or more employees.
2. The Local Committee is constituted by the District Officer.
3. The Act covers domestic workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
Domestic workers are covered; complaints by them go to the Local Committee.

questions.q: A factory with 320 workers closes one department and terminates 40 workers, offering compensation but without approaching the government. Under the IR Code, the termination is:
o: Illegal, since retrenchment in establishments with 300 or more workers needs prior permission
Legal, since prior permission is needed only for 1,000 or more workers
Legal, as departmental closure is never retrenchment
questions.x: Chapter X applies to factories, mines and plantations with 300 or more workers; retrenchment without prior permission is illegal and workers are deemed in service.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): In Excel Wear (1978) the Supreme Court struck down the then Section 25-O of the ID Act.
Reason (R): The Court held that the right to close a business is an aspect of the right to carry on business under Article 19(1)(g).
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The unguided power to refuse permission for closure was held to be an unreasonable restriction.

questions.q: An HR manager finds that higher pay reduces dissatisfaction but does not create enthusiasm; recognition and challenging work do. This is explained by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Herzberg's two-factor theory. Pay is a hygiene factor; recognition and achievement are motivators.

questions.q: Which case is the leading authority that the domestic inquiry must follow natural justice even when standing orders provide for automatic termination for overstaying leave?
o: D. K. Yadav v. J.M.A. Industries (1993)
questions.x: Correct answer: D. K. Yadav v. J.M.A. Industries (1993). The Court read natural justice into Article 21 for termination.

questions.q: In a dispute over a dismissed worker, the Industrial Tribunal finds the misconduct proved but the punishment disproportionate. It may:
o: Refer the case back to the employer without any order
Substitute a lesser punishment and give consequential relief
Only order reinstatement with full back wages
questions.x: The power earlier in Section 11A of the ID Act is retained in the IR Code.

questions.q:
Consider the following about contract labour under the OSH Code, 2020:
1. Provisions apply to establishments or contractors employing fifty or more contract workers.
2. Contract labour in core activities is prohibited, subject to specified exceptions.
3. The principal employer has no obligation even if the contractor fails to provide welfare facilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The principal employer must provide welfare facilities if the contractor fails, and may recover the cost.

questions.q: A 52-year-old bank account holder wants both life cover (any cause) and accident cover under government micro-insurance schemes. Which is correct?
o: She can join PMSBY but not PMJJBY, since PMJJBY enrolment is up to age 50
questions.x: Correct answer: She can join PMSBY but not PMJJBY, since PMJJBY enrolment is up to age 50. PMJJBY enrolment age is 18–50 (cover till 55); PMSBY is 18–70.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Employees' Pension Scheme, 1995:
1. It is a defined benefit scheme funded by the employer's 8.33% and the Central Government's 1.16%.
2. Members contribute nothing directly from their wages to EPS in the normal course.
3. Pension is payable only if the member has completed twenty years of service.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Monthly pension requires ten years of eligible service; twenty years earns a weightage of two years.

questions.q: A woman employee entitled to 26 weeks of maternity benefit has an average daily wage of ₹700. Following the Supreme Court's view in B. Shah v. Presiding Officer (1977) that the benefit covers all days of the period, the total maternity benefit is:
questions.x:
The benefit is paid for every day of the 26-week period including Sundays: 26 × 7 = 182 days.
Amount = ₹700 × 182 = ₹1,27,400. (Using 6 days/week would wrongly give ₹1,09,200.)

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹21,000 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 21,000 = ₹2,520.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 2,520 − 1,250 = ₹1,270.

questions.q:
Consider the following about maternity protection in India:
1. Under the Maternity Benefit Act, an establishment with 50 or more employees must provide a creche.
2. Work from home after maternity benefit may be allowed by mutual agreement where the work permits.
3. PMMVY gives ₹5,000 for the first child and, under PMMVY 2.0, ₹6,000 for a second child if it is a girl.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following about Atal Pension Yojana:
1. Income-tax payers have not been allowed to join since October 2022.
2. It assures a fixed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 from age 60.
3. The pension depends only on market returns, without any guarantee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The Government guarantees the chosen pension amount.

questions.q: An EPF member in continuous service dies. Average monthly wages over the last 12 months were ₹12,000 and the average balance in the member's PF account over that period was ₹1,00,000. The assurance benefit under the EDLI Scheme is:
questions.x:
EDLI = 35 × average monthly wages (ceiling ₹15,000) + 50% of the average PF balance (bonus capped at ₹1,75,000), subject to a minimum of ₹2.5 lakh and a maximum of ₹7 lakh.
35 × 12,000 = ₹4,20,000; bonus = min(50% × 1,00,000, 1,75,000) = ₹50,000.
Total ₹4,70,000.

questions.q: Arrange the following EPF interest rates by financial year, from earliest to latest: 1. 8.10% 2. 8.15% 3. 8.25% (first year it was declared) 4. 8.50%
An employer with 30 employees each earning ₹12,000 (basic + DA) pays EPF contributions. The total monthly employer outgo towards EPF, EPS, EDLI and administrative charges (0.50%) is:

Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The National Social Assistance Programme gives effect to a Directive Principle.
Reason (R): Article 41 asks the State to provide public assistance in cases of old age, sickness and disablement.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. NSAP was launched in 1995.

questions.q:
Consider the following about operating systems:
1. They manage memory, processes, files and devices.
2. Android is based on the Linux kernel.
3. An operating system is an example of application software.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The OS is system software.

questions.q:
Match the household substance with its chemical:
Substance:
A. Baking soda
B. Washing soda
C. Bleaching powder
D. Plaster of Paris
Chemical:
1. Calcium sulphate hemihydrate
2. Sodium hydrogen carbonate
3. Sodium carbonate decahydrate
4. Calcium oxychloride
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Baking soda) → 2 (Sodium hydrogen carbonate); B (Washing soda) → 3 (Sodium carbonate decahydrate); C (Bleaching powder) → 4 (Calcium oxychloride); D (Plaster of Paris) → 1 (Calcium sulphate hemihydrate).
Each is used commonly at home or in construction.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the CPU:
1. The control unit directs the operation of the processor.
2. The arithmetic logic unit carries out arithmetic and logical operations.
3. The clock speed alone fully determines a processor's performance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Performance also depends on cores, cache, architecture and instructions per cycle.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the decibel scale:
1. An increase of 10 dB means a tenfold increase in sound intensity.
2. Long exposure to sound above about 85 dB can damage hearing.
3. The decibel scale is linear.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
The scale is logarithmic.

questions.q:
Consider the following about lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries:
1. Sodium is far more abundant and cheaper than lithium.
2. Sodium-ion cells generally have lower energy density than lithium-ion cells.
3. Sodium-ion cells cannot be recharged.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Both are rechargeable chemistries.

questions.q:
Consider the following about biological nitrogen fixation:
1. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in root nodules of legumes.
2. Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium.
3. Blue-green algae are used as biofertiliser in paddy fields.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
All three are correct.

questions.q:
Match the type of machine learning with an example:
Type:
A. Supervised learning
B. Unsupervised learning
C. Reinforcement learning
D. Transfer learning
Example:
1. A program learning a game through rewards
2. Grouping customers by buying patterns
3. Predicting loan default from labelled past records
4. Adapting a pre-trained model to a new task
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.x:
Correct matching — A (Supervised learning) → 3 (Predicting loan default from labelled past records); B (Unsupervised learning) → 2 (Grouping customers by buying patterns); C (Reinforcement learning) → 1 (A program learning a game through rewards); D (Transfer learning) → 4 (Adapting a pre-trained model to a new task).
Each approach learns from data differently.

questions.q:
Consider the following about iron in the diet:
1. Vitamin C improves absorption of iron from plant foods.
2. Tea or coffee taken with meals can reduce iron absorption.
3. Plant foods contain haem iron, which is absorbed better than iron from meat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Haem iron is found in meat; plant foods contain non-haem iron, which is absorbed less well.

questions.q: A person stands in a closed car during a thunderstorm and the car is struck by lightning. Why is the person usually safe?
o: Charge stays on the outer metal body, which acts as a Faraday cage
Rubber tyres insulate the car from the ground
The car's battery neutralises the charge
The glass windows absorb the charge
questions.x: The common belief about tyres is wrong; the metal shell carries the current around the occupants.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): MRI scans do not expose patients to ionising radiation.
Reason (R): MRI uses strong magnetic fields and radio waves to image the body.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. X-rays and CT scans use ionising radiation.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): A 'digital arrest' call is a fraud.
Reason (R): No law enforcement agency in India arrests people over video calls.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Fraudsters pose as officials to extort money.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the corrosion of iron:
1. Rusting needs both oxygen and water.
2. Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which corrodes in preference to iron.
3. Rust is mainly anhydrous iron(II) oxide.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Rust is mainly hydrated iron(III) oxide.

questions.q: Cells A1 to A4 contain 10, 20, 30 and 40. What does =COUNTIF(A1:A4, ">20") return?
questions.x: Only 30 and 40 are greater than 20.

questions.q: A train 240 m long running at 72 km/h crosses a platform in 35 seconds. The length of the platform is:
questions.x:
Speed = 72 × 5/18 = 20 m/s. Distance covered in 35 s = 700 m = train + platform.
Platform = 700 − 240 = 460 m.

questions.q: The membership of a cooperative society rises by 50%, then falls by 20%, and finally rises by 5%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 50/100) × (1 − 20/100) × (1 + 5/100) = 1.5 × 0.8 × 1.05 = 1.26.
Overall change = (1.26 − 1) × 100 = 26% → 26% increase.
Note: simply adding (50 − 20 + 5) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q:
Members enrolled in a district (thousand) — 2020: 290  |  2021: 350  |  2022: 345  |  2023: 340  |  2024: 360.
What is the percentage change from 2022 to 2023?
questions.x:
Change = 340 − 345 = -5 on a base of 345 (earlier year).
% change = -5/345 × 100 = -1.45% → 1.45% decrease.

questions.q: In a certain code, 'A − B' means A is the brother of B; 'A % B' means A is the daughter of B; 'A × B' means A is the husband of B. If 'M % Q % K' (read as M % Q and Q % K), how is M related to K?
questions.x:
M % Q: M is the daughter of Q. Q % K: Q is the daughter of K.
Combining the two (all persons taken to be of one family, as is conventional): M is the granddaughter of K.

questions.q: In a row, Rahul is 17th from the left and Rekha is 10th from the right. When they interchange their positions, Rahul becomes 34th from the left. How many persons are there in the row?
questions.x:
After interchange, Rahul occupies Rekha's old place, which is 10th from the right and now 34th from the left.
Total = 34 + 10 − 1 = 43.

questions.q: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock will the hands of a clock coincide?
questions.x:
At 2:00 the minute hand is 10 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To coincide it must gain 10 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 10 × 60/55 = 120/11 minutes = 10 10/11 minutes past 2.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'MINIMUM' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 420 (M appears 3 times, I appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 20 × 3 = 60.
Not all together = 420 − 60 = 360.

questions.q: A vessel holds 30 litres of pure milk. 6 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 30 × (1 − 6/30)² = 30 × (0.8)² = 19.2 litres.
Removing 2 × 6 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 7 : 5. After 15 years, the ratio will become 5 : 4. What is P's present age?
The average of 11 observations is 57. The average of the first 6 is 53 and that of the last 6 is 56. The 6th observation is:
questions.x:
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 57 = 627.
First 6 + last 6 = 6×53 + 6×56 = 654; the middle observation is counted twice.
Middle = 654 − 627 = 27.

questions.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into cones of base radius 3 cm and height 2 cm. How many cones are obtained?
questions.x:
Number = volume of sphere / volume of one cone = (4/3)πR³ / ((1/3)πr²h)
= 4R³ / (r²h) = 4 × 6³ / (3² × 2) = 864 / 18 = 48.

questions.q: An article is marked 40% above its cost. Two successive discounts of 20% and 5% are then given on the marked price. The resulting gain or loss per cent is:
questions.x:
Take CP = 100 → MP = 140.
After 20%: 112; after a further 5%: 106.4.
Net = 106.4 − 100 = 6.4 → 6.4% gain.
Successive discounts are multiplied, never added (20% + 5% ≠ 25%).

questions.q: Two trains start at the same time from stations X and Y towards each other. After they cross, they take 100 hours and 9 hours respectively to reach Y and X. The ratio of the speed of the train from X to that of the train from Y is:
questions.x:
Standard result: S₁ : S₂ = √t₂ : √t₁, where t₁ and t₂ are the times taken after meeting.
= √9 : √100 = 3 : 10 = 3 : 10.

questions.q: A surveyor starts from point O and walks 17 km towards South, then turns left and walks 21 km, then turns left and walks 29 km, and finally turns left and walks 26 km. What is the shortest distance and direction of the final position from O?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -17 +29 = 12 km → 12 km North.
East–West: +21 -26 = -5 km → 5 km West.
Distance = √(5² + 12²) = 13 km, towards North-West.
